title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
weeklyTopics: Language Models cont'd, Text Categorization and Evaluation, Naive Bayes, Part-of-Speech
Machine Learning Basics, Neural Networks, Formal Grammars of English
workloadNotes: Four assignments (60% total, 15% each), a team project of 2-3 students (35% total: proposal, mid-term and final reports, presentation, and peer feedback), and participation (5%). 8 total late days budget for the semester (20 points/100 penalty per late day beyond that); late days not applicable to the final presentation.
prerequisitesText: Senior undergraduate level; proficiency in a programming language (Python recommended), courses in algorithms, probability, and statistics; linear algebra and prior ML exposure recommended but not required.
textbooks: Dan Jurafsky and James H. Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 2009 (main; 3rd ed. draft freely available online)
Jacob Eisenstein, Introduction to Natural Language Processing, MIT Press, 2019 (reference)
Chris Manning and Hinrich Schutze, Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing, MIT Press, 1999 (reference)
